thread.title: From automotive to robotics, 5 innovations that will spur growth at Jabil

author: Margie Manning
title: From automotive to robotics, 5 innovations that will spur growth at Jabil
text: – Finance Editor, Tampa Bay Business Journal Jan 26, 2018, 7:38am EST Self-driving cars, super-fast wireless service and smart factories are among the technologies that will prove most fruitful for Jabil Inc. in the future. Mark Mondello, CEO of St. Petersburg-based Jabil (NYSE: JBL), came up with his short list for most promising innovations, during the electronic service company’s annual shareholders meeting Thursday. Currently, Apple Inc . (NASDAQ: AAPL) is Jabil’s biggest customer, accounting for about 24 percent of the company’s $19.1 billion in revenue in fiscal 2017. “What is the next Apple for you guys?” a shareholder asked during the meeting. “I don’t know that I think about any one particular customer or one product being the next biggest thing,” Mondello said. "In fact, for shareholders I actually think the opposite. If we get to a point of taking great care of our biggest customers but at the same time we grow other areas of our business, I can see a day where no particular product, no particular customer is more than 5 to 6 percent of our business.” That could raise Jabil’s standing with research analysts and credit rating agencies, who in the past have cited concerns about high customer concentration. Mondello singled out five areas that will help Jabil grow. Automotive. “You think about not only autonomous driving and intelligent sensors, but you think about propulsion engines starting to give way to things that are very electronic oriented,” Mondello said. Energy and industrial will be “great areas” for Jabil. Base stations , which are radio receivers and transmitters that serve as the hub of the local wireless network , and may also be the gateway between a wired network and the wireless network. “Every time you turn your phone on, it connects to a wireless network unless you’re on Wi-Fi. But whether you connect to Wi-Fi or you connect to the cellular base stations, there’s a high percentage that Jabil had something to do with those products.” 5G , or fifth generation wireless technology which allows users to browse the internet, upload or download videos, and use data-intensive apps or features such as virtual reality much more quickly and smoothly than is possible now, according to Motley Fool . “The entire Wi-Fi network has gone from 2G to 2.5G to 3G to 4G to LTE, and 5G is going to open up the markets to lots of different technologies that need to operate without latency and with enhanced speed. We’re participating in that, so 5G wireless network is an area that will be quite good for us,” Mondello said. Smart factories. Jabil has 100 sites in 29 countries with the 42 million square feet of manufacturing space, and Mondello said while he’s proud of those facilities, not all of the factories are the best in the world. “I want to see a day where all our factories are the best factories in terms of smart factories, intelligence and robotics. So another area that will be big is robotics, automation, data analytics and digital,” he said. At next year’s shareholders meeting, he said there likely will be an update on the progress Jabil has made in its factories. “Those are the areas I think about that in the next two to three years will drive importance and good valuation for the company,” Mondello said.
